objective: Learners compute an advertised percentage discount from invented prices and test a vaguer advertising claim against the arithmetic.
scenario: Delphine is an invented fifth grader looking at a pretend advertisement for a $45.00 jacket. The invented banner says 20% off today, while the headline shouts practically half price. All prices and claims are invented for checking.
safetyNotes: Every amount, person, business, and account in this task is invented for practice. Nothing here refers to a real household.
Never write a real bank account, card, PIN, password, Social Security, or tax number on this sheet; the task never asks for one.
This is education, not individualized financial advice. Real money decisions belong to a trusted adult.

tasks.directions: Apply the invented 20% discount to Delphine's $45.00 jacket.

prompts.text: How much does the 20% discount take off?

tasks.directions: Work out what Delphine actually pays, then work out what half price would have been so the two can be compared.

prompts.text: What would a true half-price jacket cost?

tasks.directions: Compare the headline claim with the actual offer, then check what the same discount does on a $60.00 invented coat.

prompts.text: How far is the real discounted price from a true half price?
What would a $60.00 coat cost after the same 20% off?

tasks.directions: The banner and the headline described the same offer.

prompts.text: The banner was accurate and the headline was not. Why would an advertisement put both on the same page?

remediation: When a learner subtracts the percentage as dollars, work 20% of $100.00 for Delphine first, then apply the same reasoning to the $45.00 price.
extension: Ask the learner what percentage off would make the headline honest for Delphine's jacket, and to prove it.
